title: Chapter 34: The Stalk of Grass 2
content:
Chapter 34

"Of course she is," Wei Wuxian whispered back with an easy smirk. "I wedged my boot straight into the doorframe—she couldn't shut it if she tried. If she hadn't let us in, I was kicking it off its hinges anyway."

Jin Ling stared at him in deadpan disbelief.

Yi City was already dripping with foul, uncanny air, and anyone living here was definitely far from ordinary. Looking at this creepy old woman had the disciples’ guts twisting into knots. They were thoroughly repulsed by the idea of stepping across that threshold, but caught between a rock and a hard place, they had to gamble. Hoisting their stiff, poisoned companions, they shuffled into the dark parlor one by one. The old woman watched them with cold, dead eyes, slamming the door shut the second the last boy crossed over.

Pitch-black darkness swallowed the room once more.

"Shopkeeper, why keep the lanterns dark?" Wei Wuxian called out.

"Lantern’s on the table," the old woman wheezed. "Light it yourselves."

Lan Sizhui happened to be standing right beside a wooden table. Groping through the gloom, his fingers brushed against a cold ceramic oil lamp, coming away coated in a thick layer of greasy dust. Slipping a fire talisman from his sleeve, he blew a spark to ignite the paper.

He leaned down to touch the flame to the wick, his eyes casually flicking across the room.

In that split second, an icy jolt shot from the soles of his feet straight to the crown of his skull, turning his scalp instantly numb.

The entire parlor was crammed wall to wall, shoulder to shoulder, packed with a sea of silent figures—every single one of them staring back at him with wide, unblinking eyes!
